clue.text: Relax wearing brother's garments

indicators.note: the brother's letters have the relaxing word on them, as a person wears clothes

parts.note: BR is the standard abbreviation for brother, with the possessive S
to laze is to relax

explanation.surface: A sibling lounges about in clothes borrowed from his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Blazers are jackets, so they are garments, often worn as part of a school or club uniform.

clue.text: Plot suspect forced, after turning, to reveal

indicators.note: the letters picked out are read backwards once they have been turned round
the run of letters is revealed within the words suspect forced

explanation.surface: A suspect is coerced into confessing a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reveal' shows TFORC across 'suspecT FORCed', and 'after turning' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented plot of farmland, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Date after end of Feb with a girl

parts.note: the day after February ends is the first of March, written MAR I with a Roman one

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a date at the start of March with a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The day after February ends is 1 March, written MAR plus I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a common female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Gloomy valley to the left covered with stones

parts.note: grave means serious or gloomy

indicators.note: in an across clue, going to the left means reading backwards

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: A sombre valley lies off to the left, strewn with rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' turns DELL into LLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravelled path or drive has been surfaced with small stones.

clue.text: Less careful, like bank after end of crash

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word crash is taken

parts.note: as means like, in the way of
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: A driver going too fast ends up crashing into a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting more hastily means acting with less care, so the comparative fits.

clue.text: Largely factual article about year's absence from school

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: true means factual
an is the indefinite article
C stands for circa, Latin for about
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A mostly accurate report deals with a pupil missing a year of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Truancy is staying away from school without permission.

clue.text: Chicken school friend stuffed with butter?

indicators.note: the school letters are filled with the butter word, as a bird is stuffed

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter; the query flags the unusual sense
cock is old British slang for a mate or friend

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs a chicken with butter, as a schoolfriend watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed with' fills the school letters with the butter word. 'Cock' as a friendly term of address ('wotcher, cock') is old Cockney slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatchcock is a chicken split open and flattened for grilling.

clue.text: Young people humorously greeting, US-style, old female

parts.note: yo is an American slang greeting

explanation.surface: Teenagers jokingly hail an elderly woman in an American manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoof is a jokey British spelling imitating a slangy way of saying youth, meaning young people.

clue.text: Place, just the thing in centre of Montserrat

indicators.note: the word for the perfect thing goes inside the middle letters
the two central letters of the ten-letter island name are taken

parts.note: it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the ideal spot in the heart of a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Montserrat is a Caribbean island; its name has ten letters, so its centre is a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or place where something stands.

clue.text: Assume homework set about revolutionary American

indicators.note: the homework and set words go around the turned American letters

parts.note: prep is British school slang for homework

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to pose a question is to set it

explanation.surface: A teacher sets homework about a revolutionary American figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the American letters round; 'about' has homework and set go around them. Prep is British boarding-school homework.
explanation.definitionFit: To presuppose is to take something for granted beforehand, that is, to assume it.

clue.text: Inconsistent food served by Greek character

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
table can mean the food served, as in 'keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A Greek waiter serves food of variable quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutable is changeable, hence inconsistent.

clue.text: Fighting against dynasty hotting up

parts.note: war is fighting
the Ming dynasty ruled China

explanation.surface: Combat against an old Chinese dynasty is intensifying.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming means heating, so it is a synonym of hotting up.

clue.text: Patient fellow delighted, we hear, about workplace

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure famed for patience

indicators.note: the word for delighted is heard but written another way

parts.note: sent means thrilled or carried away
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A patient man is overjoyed about finding a place to work.
explanation.walkthrough: A JOBCENTRE is the British government office that helps people find work.
explanation.definitionFit: A jobcentre is a place for finding jobs, playing on workplace as a place connected with work.

clue.text: This often accompanies speaker's thanks, for a start

definitions.text: This often accompanies speaker's thanks, for a start

parts.words: This often accompanies speaker's thanks, for a start
parts.note: an after-dinner speaker who thanks the hosts usually ends by asking guests to raise glasses, while for a start points to breakfast fare

explanation.surface: A speaker opens with words of gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is drunk after a speech, and toasted bread is a breakfast starter.

clue.text: Temperature taken by doctor, hard to get accurate

indicators.note: the temperature letter is taken on by the doctor and hard letters

parts.note: to doctor is to rig or falsify
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a patient's temperature, struggling to get the reading accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct, so it is a synonym for accurate.

clue.text: Sound angry about priest needing help from others

indicators.note: the rant word goes around the priest's name

parts.note: to rant is to sound off angrily
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: Someone shouts furiously at a priest who requires assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reliant means depending on others for support.

clue.text: Waiter with Italian port guy's not finished

parts.note: Bari is a port on Italy's Adriatic coast

indicators.note: the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a guy is a rope or stay steadying a tent or mast

explanation.surface: A waiter in an Italian port town has not finished his shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of guy's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista serves coffee in a café, so a loose kind of waiter.

clue.text: Captain treated by hospital in an emergency

indicators.note: the letters are processed or worked over, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is treated at a hospital after an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch is an idiom meaning if really necessary, in an emergency.

clue.text: Keen to be getting on among mounted troops

indicators.note: the ageing word goes among the letters of the troops
in a down clue, mounted means turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of troops
to age is to be getting on in years

explanation.surface: An old soldier is keen to ride with the cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns the troops' letters upward, as in a down clue, and 'among' puts the ageing word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen, enthusiastic.

clue.text: South Africa copper's landing role in film

indicators.note: the abbreviation for South Africa lands or catches the role, holding it

parts.note: a part is a role
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A South African policeman gets a part in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal Cu. Spartacus is the 1960 Kubrick film.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus is the title of a well-known film about the slave revolt.

clue.text: Means of payment Red Queen used oddly

parts.note: Che Guevara was a famous communist, a Red

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's Red Queen pays in an odd way.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money.

clue.text: Yellow light over Florida location

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
to light on is to land, as a bird alights
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A yellow lamp shines over a spot in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is a city in central Florida.

clue.text: Drink makes you extremely tipsy, with rum in

indicators.note: the strange word goes inside the outer letters
only the two extreme letters of tipsy are taken

parts.note: rum means odd or strange in British slang

explanation.surface: A drink that leaves you very tipsy when rum is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives TY from 'tipsy'; 'rum' means odd, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: First of emotions politician experiences is stress

indicators.note: only the opening letter of emotions is taken

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
to have, has, is to experience

explanation.surface: A politician feeling emotional is under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is stress laid on a word or point.

clue.text: Ooh vicar — this will hide your bloomers!

definitions.text: Ooh vicar — this will hide your bloomers!

parts.words: Ooh vicar — this will hide your bloomers!
parts.note: the camp seaside-postcard tone suggests underwear, but bloomers are blunders, and a fluid that covers written mistakes hides them

explanation.surface: A saucy remark to a vicar about covering up underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers are both women's knickers and blunders; the product meant hides writing errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Correction fluid, a corrector, paints over written mistakes.

clue.text: Transports her gifts abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread about

explanation.surface: Someone ships her presents overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To freight goods is to transport them as cargo.

clue.text: Show up at the empty theatre, love

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole run is read backwards
the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
O is love, a score of nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A lover turns up at a theatre with nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: AT, TE (the emptied), REP and O are read backwards as one.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, a kind of stage show.

clue.text: Announced Spooner's name for sailing vessel — carrier

indicators.note: the first sounds of the two words are swapped as Dr Spooner would say them aloud

parts.note: a boat is a sailing vessel
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: Dr Spooner names a ship, his slip producing a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BOAT TAG gives a phrase spoken like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote bag is a large open bag for carrying things.

clue.text: Agent the west picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: the Occident is the western world

explanation.surface: A secret agent is overheard in the western world.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidant is a chemical agent that oxidizes other substances.

clue.text: Like pupils in top stream revising tables

indicators.note: revising means altering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bright students are revising their times tables.
explanation.walkthrough: A stream is a British school's ability group.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in the top stream are the most able in their year.

clue.text: Important judge probes New Zealander, failing to reach conclusion

indicators.note: the judge letter probes, pushing inside the other word
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Maori is a native New Zealander

explanation.surface: A senior judge interrogates a New Zealander but reaches no verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means important or significant.

clue.text: Here we go — left turn

parts.note: whee is the cry of someone setting off on a thrill ride

explanation.surface: A driver cries out excitedly while making a left turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round, as a column of soldiers wheels.
